newsitem.title: USA: Five killed in New Mexico plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in New Mexico plane crash.

text.p: Five people were killed when their Piper Comanche aircraft crashed in a field between houses in the town of Farmington late Friday, police said.

The six-seater plane flew only a mile from Farmington Airport, about 140 miles northwest of Albuquerque, before it plunged into the field at around 11:15 P.M. Mountain Time (1:15 A.M. EST Saturday), police said.

"The plane's engine cut off suddenly and the plane nose-dived," Lt. Glenn Thomas of the New Mexico State Police said. The victims, believed to be three women and two men from the Albuquerque area, died on impact, he said.
"It was engulfed in flames, I don't think anyone had a chance," Brian Barrowclough, whose house overlooks the field, said.
Other eyewitnesses told police the pilot made a desperate attempt to crash land in one of the few open spaces in this residential area.
Investigators from the Federal Aviation Administration sorted through the plane's wreckage Saturday morning in an attempt to identify the victims and the cause of the crash.
